literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 值得注意的是,LNP@NP-PROTAC#4在体外和体内均展现出显著的抗病毒药物活性。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2721813]
与 AlphaMissense 的比较揭示了预测非结构化 N 末端基序和脂质嵌入域内变体影响的系统局限性。 [10.1038/s42003-026-10800-0]

克隆 4F02 识别了传播数十年的人类甲型流感 (H3N2) 病毒的 HA。它能中和多种 H3N2 病毒,表现出微弱的血凝抑制作用,阻断 HA 介导的融合活性,激活 Fc 受体介导的信号传导,并保护小鼠免受致命攻击。冷冻电镜显示,4F02 靶向位于头-茎界面处的 HA 头基部,跨越抗原位点 C、D 和 E。在人类血清中检测到了针对类似表位的抗体,尽管水平较低。 [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106450]
研究在分支K变异株的血凝素(HA)蛋白中识别出多个突变,包括抗原位点A、B、D区域及受体结合位点(RBS)的关键替换[A1]。 [10.1002/mco2.70953]
在23,278份呼吸道样本中,1,003份(4.31%)甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09检测阳性,季节性高峰主要出现在流行病学周第13至16周。系统发育分析显示病毒谱系持续替换,2015年后3C.2a衍生分支占主导地位。 [10.20944/preprints202608.1453.v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Importantly, LNP@NP-PROTAC#4 demonstrated potent antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo. [10.1080/21505594.2026.2721813]
Comparison with AlphaMissense reveals systematic limitations in predicting the effects of variants within unstructured N-terminal motifs and lipid-embedded domains. [10.1038/s42003-026-10800-0]

Clone 4F02 recognised the HA of human influenza A (H3N2) viruses that circulated across multiple decades. It neutralised multiple H3N2 viruses, exhibited weak haemagglutination inhibition, blocked HA-mediated fusion activity, activated Fc receptor-mediated signalling, and protected mice against lethal challenge. [10.1016/j.ebiom.2026.106450]

The study identified multiple mutations in the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of the subclade K variants, including key substitutions in regions of antigenic sites A, B, and D, as well as the receptor binding site (RBS) [A1]. [10.1002/mco2.70953]

Among 729 patients with laboratory-confirmed A(H1N1)pdm09 infection, 21.7% (158/729) developed pneumonia. Among those with pneumonia, 36.7% developed moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, 15.2% required invasive ventilation, 48.7% were admitted to the ICU, and 8.2% died. [10.1371/journal.pone.0348450]

Former WHO Chief Scientist Dr. Soumya Swaminathan stated that the current increase in H1N1 cases is a seasonal influenza uptick, not due to a new strain. Doctors report an increase in H1N1 influenza cases and symptoms in Delhi, India, with a focus on fever, cough, and cold-like symptoms. The event is confirmed through medical observations and testing. [news-5d28453a1ba80c6f]

Health authorities in Bhopal have increased surveillance for seasonal influenza, including H1N1, after three H1N1 cases were reported in the city over the past week, bringing the total number of cases in August to six. [news-7353ec17c6fb68e0]

papers.title: Adaptive Advantage of the Emerging Seasonal Influenza A (H3N2) Subclade K: Enhanced Receptor Binding Capacity and Immune Escape Potential
papers.abstract: Emerging influenza variants continue to drive waves of flu globally.Notably, the influenza A (H3N2) subclade K (J.2.4.1) is currently the dominant strain during the 2025-2026 Northern Hemisphere influenza season, spreading rapidly across Asia, Europe, and North America [ 1 ].These variants exhibit multiple mutations in the hemagglutinin (HA) protein, including key substitutions in regions of antigenic sites A, B, and D, as well as the receptor binding site (RBS) (Figure 1A ).Notably, glycosylation changes at positions 135 (loss) and 144 (gain) may contribute to its enhanced adaptability.The rapid spread of subclade K, along with early reports of flu outbreaks in countries such as Japan, the United Kingdom (UK) and the United States (USA), has prompted public health agencies to prioritize surveillance and vaccine updates [ 2,3 ].However, the biological characteristics of the newly emerging subclade K remain unclear.In this study, we retrieved all available HA sequences of influenza A (H3N2) virus belonging to clade J (2a.3a.1) from the Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) platform.These sequences were geographically sourced from Asia, Europe, and North America, spanning the period from June 6, 2020 to January 16, 2026.A total of 62,080 HA sequences were obtained, including 11,014 sequences from the 2025-2026 influenza season.Among these, 9,795 (88.93%) were classified as subclade K.We randomly selected 5 viral sequences from each subclade (J, J.1, J.2, J.2.2, J.2.4, K) in each region of the three areas, totaling 90 viral sequences for the study of biological characteristics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Emerging influenza variants continue to drive waves of flu globally. Notably, the influenza A (H3N2) subclade K (J.2.4.1) is currently the dominant strain during the 2025-2026 Northern Hemisphere influenza season, spreading rapidly across Asia, Europe, and North America [A1].
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study retrieved all available HA sequences of influenza A (H3N2) virus belonging to clade J (2a.3a.1) from the GISAID platform, geographically sourced from Asia, Europe, and North America, spanning the period from June 6, 2020 to January 16, 2026 [A1]. A total of 62,080 HA sequences were obtained, including 11,014 sequences from the 2025-2026 influenza season. Among these, 9,795 (88.93%) were classified as subclade K.
analysis.methods: The study randomly selected 5 viral sequences from each subclade (J, J.1, J.2, J.2.2, J.2.4, K) in each region of the three areas, totaling 90 viral sequences for the study of biological characteristics [A1].
analysis.main_results: The study identified multiple mutations in the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of the subclade K variants, including key substitutions in regions of antigenic sites A, B, and D, as well as the receptor binding site (RBS) [A1].
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these mutations as potentially contributing to the enhanced adaptability of subclade K, which may explain its rapid spread and immune escape potential [A1].
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for updated surveillance and vaccine strategies to address the evolving characteristics of subclade K, which is currently the dominant strain in the 2025-2026 influenza season [A1].
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on sequence data from the GISAID platform, which may not fully represent all circulating strains. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the analysis [A1].

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the biological characteristics of the emerging influenza A (H3N2) subclade K, which is currently the dominant strain during the 2025-2026 Northern Hemisphere influenza season. The research highlights the multiple mutations in the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of subclade K variants, particularly in antigenic sites A, B, and D, as well as the receptor binding site (RBS). These mutations may contribute to the subclade's enhanced adaptability and immune escape potential, which could explain its rapid spread across Asia, Europe, and North America. The study retrieved HA sequences from GISAID, spanning from June 2020 to January 2026, and randomly selected 90 sequences for analysis. The findings suggest the need for updated surveillance and vaccine strategies to address the evolving nature of subclade K. However, the study is limited by its reliance on sequence data and the observational nature of the analysis, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Morbidity and mortality burden of seasonal influenza in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza poses a significant global health burden, responsible for substantial morbidity and mortality annually, particularly among high-risk populations such as the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and individuals with chronic illnesses. While the burden of influenza is well-documented in high-income countries, limited data exist for sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries, where fragile healthcare systems and underreporting obscure the true impact. Influenza exacerbates prevalent health conditions such as HIV, malaria, and malnutrition, further increasing its toll. The meta-analysis outlined in this protocol aims to systematically assess the morbidity and mortality burden of seasonal influenza in SSA countries, providing policymakers with critical insights to strengthen surveillance, prioritize at-risk populations, and inform vaccination strategies. This is a protocol for a planned systematic review and meta-analysis. This research will follow the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, incorporating observational studies and surveillance reports published between August 2010 and December 2026. We will search major health databases, including MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, as well as regional databases (African Index Medicus and the WHO Global Index Medicus) and grey literature sources (medRxiv and national health reports). Studies reporting laboratory-confirmed seasonal influenza cases from SSA countries will be included. A standardized form will be used for data extraction, capturing morbidity (prevalence, incidence, and hospitalization rates) and mortality (case-fatality rates and excess mortality rates) indicators. Pooled data will be analyzed using meta-analytic techniques, applying random-effects models to account for heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses will address variations in case definitions, methodologies, and study quality across studies. Publication and language bias will be mitigated by including grey literature and applying no language restrictions. The completed review is expected to provide updated, pooled estimates of seasonal influenza-associated morbidity and mortality across SSA countries, stratified by age group, geographic subregion, and presence of comorbidities. These findings will support evidence-based policy decisions, including the strengthening of influenza surveillance systems and the prioritization of vaccination programs for high-risk populations in SSA countries. As this study involves secondary data from published literature, ethical approval is not required. Results will be disseminated via a peer-reviewed publication, conference presentations, and stakeholder meetings. Tailored reports will be shared with policymakers in SSA countries to translate findings into public health strategies, particularly to enhance surveillance and implement targeted vaccination programs. PROSPERO CRD42024617707

papers.title_zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲地区 季节性流感 的发病率和 死亡率 负担:系统评价和荟萃分析方案
papers.source_body_en: Seasonal influenza poses a significant global health burden, responsible for substantial morbidity and mortality annually, particularly among high-risk populations such as the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and individuals with chronic illnesses. While the burden of influenza is well-documented in high-income countries, limited data exist for sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries, where fragile healthcare systems and underreporting obscure the true impact. Influenza exacerbates prevalent health conditions such as HIV, malaria, and malnutrition, further increasing its toll. The meta-analysis outlined in this protocol aims to systematically assess the morbidity and mortality burden of seasonal influenza in SSA countries, providing policymakers with critical insights to strengthen surveillance, prioritize at-risk populations, and inform vaccination strategies. This is a protocol for a planned systematic review and meta-analysis. This research will follow the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, incorporating observational studies and surveillance reports published between August 2010 and December 2026. We will search major health databases, including MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, as well as regional databases (African Index Medicus and the WHO Global Index Medicus) and grey literature sources (medRxiv and national health reports). Studies reporting laboratory-confirmed seasonal influenza cases from SSA countries will be included. A standardized form will be used for data extraction, capturing morbidity (prevalence, incidence, and hospitalization rates) and mortality (case-fatality rates and excess mortality rates) indicators. Pooled data will be analyzed using meta-analytic techniques, applying random-effects models to account for heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses will address variations in case definitions, methodologies, and study quality across studies. Publication and language bias will be mitigated by including grey literature and applying no language restrictions. The completed review is expected to provide updated, pooled estimates of seasonal influenza-associated morbidity and mortality across SSA countries, stratified by age group, geographic subregion, and presence of comorbidities. These findings will support evidence-based policy decisions, including the strengthening of influenza surveillance systems and the prioritization of vaccination programs for high-risk populations in SSA countries. As this study involves secondary data from published literature, ethical approval is not required. Results will be disseminated via a peer-reviewed publication, conference presentations, and stakeholder meetings. Tailored reports will be shared with policymakers in SSA countries to translate findings into public health strategies, particularly to enhance surveillance and implement targeted vaccination programs. PROSPERO CRD42024617707
papers.abstract_zh: 季节性流感对全球健康构成重大负担,每年导致大量发病率和死亡率,尤其是在高风险人群中,如老年人、婴幼儿、孕妇和患有慢性疾病的个体。尽管流感在高收入国家的负担已被充分记录,但撒哈拉以南非洲(SSA)国家的数据却十分有限,脆弱的医疗体系和报告不足掩盖了其真实影响。流感会加重普遍存在的健康状况,如HIV、疟疾和营养不良,进一步增加其危害。本协议中概述的荟萃分析旨在系统评估季节性流感在SSA国家的发病率和死亡率负担,为政策制定者提供关键见解,以加强监测、优先考虑高风险人群,并制定疫苗接种策略。这是一项关于计划进行的系统综述和荟萃分析的协议。本研究将遵循系统综述和荟萃分析的首选报告项目(PRISMA)2020指南,纳入2010年8月至2026年12月期间发表的观察性研究和监测报告。我们将搜索主要的健康数据库,包括MEDLINE(通过PubMed)、Embase、Scopus、Web of Science和Cochrane图书馆,以及区域数据库(非洲医学索引和世界卫生组织全球医学索引)和灰色文献来源(medRxiv和国家健康报告)。将纳入来自SSA国家的实验室确诊季节性流感病例的研究。将使用标准化表格进行数据提取,记录发病率(患病率、发病率和住院率)和死亡率(病例死亡率和超额死亡率)指标。将使用荟萃分析技术对汇总数据进行分析,应用随机效应模型以考虑异质性。敏感性分析将解决不同病例定义、方法和研究质量之间的差异。通过纳入灰色文献并不限制语言,将减轻出版偏倚和语言偏倚。完成的综述预计将在SSA国家提供更新的、汇总的季节性流感相关发病率和死亡率估计,按年龄组、地理次区域和合并症的存在情况进行分层。这些发现将支持基于证据的政策决策,包括加强流感监测系统和优先考虑SSA国家高风险人群的疫苗接种项目。由于本研究涉及已发表文献的二次数据,无需伦理批准。结果将通过同行评审的出版物、会议报告和利益相关者会议进行传播。将为SSA国家的政策制定者提供定制报告,将研究结果转化为公共卫生策略,特别是增强监测并实施针对性的疫苗接种项目。PROSPERO CRD42024617707

papers.title: Deciphering influenza B virus-derived peptides and their presentation by HLA class I molecules.
papers.abstract: Despite influenza vaccines being widely available, influenza still causes significant morbidity and mortality annually. Vaccines typically induce humoral-mediated protection against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, necessitating that they be updated and administered each year. In contrast, CD8+ T cells, which can control and clear viral infections, can recognise more conserved viral epitopes. Therefore, there is considerable interest in understanding CD8+ T cell responses to influenza virus for the development of future vaccines and therapeutics. Although Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUAV) and Betainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUBV) co-circulate in humans and both contribute to seasonal epidemics, there is limited data regarding CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV. This knowledge gap spans both immunological and molecular insights. In the present review, we summarise the current knowledge of FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at both cellular and molecular levels, in comparison with FLUAV. Collectively, this highlights the limited data available on FLUBV, despite its significant role in human influenza infections.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses human seasonal influenza B virus (FLUBV) with a focus on CD8+ T cell responses to conserved epitopes, contrasting with influenza A virus (FLUAV). It highlights that current vaccines, which induce humoral responses against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, require annual updates, whereas CD8+ T cells target more conserved epitopes, offering potential for broader protection. The review synthesizes existing knowledge on FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at cellular and molecular levels, explicitly comparing FLUBV to FLUAV. It concludes that CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV are understudied, with limited data available despite FLUBV's significant role in human influenza infections. The review identifies a critical gap in understanding FLUBV-specific CD8+ T cell epitopes and their HLA class I presentation, emphasizing the need for further research to inform the development of vaccines and therapeutics leveraging conserved T cell responses.

papers.title: Phylogeographic Dynamics and Spatial Connectivity of Influenza A(H3N2) in Brazil
papers.abstract: Influenza A(H3N2) viruses show continuous antigenic and genetic evolution, requiring sustained molecular surveillance to understand their circulation and geographic spread. This study investigated the epidemiological, evolutionary, and phylogeographic dynamics of A(H3N2) viruses circulating in Brazil between 2011 and 2019. Epidemiological surveillance data from Northern and Northeastern Brazil were analyzed together with hemagglutinin (HA) gene sequences generated in this study and sequences retrieved from GISAID EpiFlu database. Phylogenetic and Bayesian phylogeographic analyses were performed to characterize genetic diversity and viral dispersal. Among 23,278 respiratory samples, 1,003 (4.31%) were positive for A(H3N2), with seasonal peaks occurring mainly between epidemiological weeks 13 and 16. Phylogenetic analyses revealed successive lineage replacement, with predominance of 3C.2a-derived clades after 2015. Phylogeographic reconstruction identified multiple international introductions into Brazil and extensive viral movement among Brazilian regions, with Southeastern Brazil acting as the main hub of national connectivity. Northern and Northeastern Brazil participated predominantly as recipient regions while also contributing to onward viral dissemination. These findings highlight the interconnected nature of A(H3N2) circulation in Brazil and reinforce the importance of integrating genomic and epidemiological surveillance to understand influenza dynamics.
authors: Edna Maria Acunã de Sousa Fillizola
Marilda Agudo Mendonça Teixeira de Siqueira

It highlights the continuous antigenic and genetic evolution of these viruses, emphasizing the need for sustained molecular surveillance. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查巴西甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09的流行病学、进化与系统地理动态,以理解其流行与地理传播,因甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09持续发生抗原漂移与遗传突变,需要持续开展分子流行病学监测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了巴西北部与东北部的流行病学监测数据,并结合本研究产生的血凝素(HA)基因序列及从GISAID EpiFlu数据库检索的序列。研究聚焦于2011年至2019年间收集的呼吸道样本。
elements_zh.methods: 开展系统发育与贝叶斯系统地理学分析以表征遗传多样性与病毒扩散。分析方法包括血凝素(HA)基因序列分析,并将其与流行病学数据整合。
elements_zh.main_results: 在23,278份呼吸道样本中,1,003份(4.31%)甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09检测阳性,季节性高峰主要出现在流行病学周第13至16周。系统发育分析显示病毒谱系持续替换,2015年后3C.2a衍生分支占主导地位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果展示甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09在巴西流行的相互连通性,其中东南部巴西作为国家连通性的主要枢纽。本研究为甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09的空间动态提供了新颖见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调整合基因组与流行病学监测以更好地理解流感动态的重要性,可为制定有针对性的公共卫生干预措施及提升未来疫情应对能力提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖流行病学监测数据与基因组序列,可能在捕捉完整病毒扩散模式方面存在局限性。然而,多源数据的整合支持研究结论具有中等可信度。

papers.title: Characterisation of a human monoclonal antibody targeting a conserved epitope at the base of the HA head of influenza A(H3N2) virus
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous broadly reactive human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against the haemagglutinin (HA) of influenza A viruses have recognised conserved epitopes across HA subtypes or within subtypes. Most heterosubtypic mAbs target the HA stem, the receptor-binding site (RBS), or the trimeric interface. Although at least three H3-specific mAbs recognise epitopes outside these regions, the overall landscape of conserved H3-specific epitopes remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify and characterise conserved epitopes on H3-HA to inform the development of vaccines resilient to antigenic change. METHODS: We screened a panel of previously reported H3-HA-reactive human mAbs to identify mAbs recognising conserved epitopes. The candidate clone, 034-10040 4F02 (4F02), was evaluated for neutralising, haemagglutination inhibiting, and HA-mediated fusion-inhibitory, Fc receptor-mediated effector functions in vitro, and for protective efficacy in a lethal mouse challenge model. Cryo-electron microscopy was used to define the structural basis of 4F02 binding. Human sera were screened for antibodies targeting similar epitopes. FINDINGS: Clone 4F02 recognised the HA of human influenza A (H3N2) viruses that circulated across multiple decades. It neutralised multiple H3N2 viruses, exhibited weak haemagglutination inhibition, blocked HA-mediated fusion activity, activated Fc receptor-mediated signalling, and protected mice against lethal challenge. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that 4F02 targets the base of the HA head at a head-stem interface spanning antigenic sites C, D, and E. Antibodies targeting similar epitopes were detected, albeit at a low level, in human sera. INTERPRETATION: Characterisation of the 4F02 epitope reveals a previously underappreciated site of vulnerability at the H3-HA head-stem interface. This finding expands our understanding of conserved epitopes and provides a target for the development of influenza vaccines resilient to antigenic change. FUNDING: This work was supported by the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development, JSPS KAKENHI, the National Institutes of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This finding provides a potential target for the development of influenza vaccines that are resilient to antigenic change, which could improve public health preparedness against seasonal influenza outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This study identifies and characterises a conserved epitope on the haemagglutinin (HA) protein of human influenza A(H3N2) viruses, revealing a previously underappreciated site of vulnerability at the HA head-stem interface. The monoclonal antibody 4F02 neutralises multiple H3N2 viruses, inhibits HA-mediated fusion, and provides protective efficacy in a mouse model. Cryo-electron microscopy defines the structural basis of 4F02 binding, and similar epitope-targeting antibodies are detected in human sera at low levels. These findings expand understanding of conserved epitopes and offer a potential target for vaccine development against antigenically changing influenza strains. The study's evidence is strong but limited to in vitro and animal models, which may affect generalisability to human populations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别并表征H3-HA上的保守表位,为开发能够抵御抗原变异的疫苗提供信息。多种广泛反应性人源单克隆抗体(mAb)已针对甲型流感病毒血凝素(HA)并识别出跨亚型或亚型内的保守表位。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究筛选了一组先前报道的针对H3-HA的反应性人源单克隆抗体,以识别能够识别保守表位的抗体。候选克隆4F02在体外被评估了中和活性、血凝抑制活性、HA介导的融合抑制活性以及Fc受体介导的效应功能,并在致死性小鼠攻击模型中评估了其保护效果。
elements_zh.methods: 我们筛选了一组先前报道的针对H3血凝素(HA)的反应性人单克隆抗体(mAb),以识别识别保守表位的mAb。使用冷冻电子显微镜确定了4F02结合的结构基础。筛选了人血清以检测针对类似表位的抗体。
elements_zh.main_results: 克隆 4F02 识别了传播数十年的人类甲型流感 (H3N2) 病毒的 HA。它能中和多种 H3N2 病毒,表现出微弱的血凝抑制作用,阻断 HA 介导的融合活性,激活 Fc 受体介导的信号传导,并保护小鼠免受致命攻击。冷冻电镜显示,4F02 靶向位于头-茎界面处的 HA 头基部,跨越抗原位点 C、D 和 E。在人类血清中检测到了针对类似表位的抗体,尽管水平较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 对4F02表位的特征分析揭示了H3-HA头部茎部接口处一个此前未被充分重视的保守性位点。该发现拓展了对保守表位的认知,并为开发针对季节性流感的疫苗疫苗提供了靶标,该疫苗对抗原变异具有更强的适应性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这一发现为开发对抗原变化具有弹性的流感 疫苗 提供了一个潜在靶标,这可以改善针对 季节性流感 暴发 的公共卫生准备。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖体外和小鼠模型数据而受到限制,这些数据可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是强有力的,因为它通过功能验证直接识别和表征了 H3-HA 上的保守表位。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:多种广谱人源单克隆抗体(mAb)已针对甲型流感病毒血凝素(HA)的保守表位展开研究,这些表位可跨越不同HA亚型或在同一亚型内保守。大多数异亚型mAb靶向HA茎部、受体结合位点(RBS)或三聚体界面。尽管至少有三种H3特异性mAb识别这些区域外的表位,但H3-HA保守表位的整体格局仍未完全明确。本研究旨在识别并表征H3-HA上的保守表位,为开发能够抵御抗原变异的疫苗提供依据。方法:筛选既往报道的H3-HA反应性人源mAb,以识别识别保守表位的mAb。候选克隆034-10040 4F02(4F02)在体外接受中和活性、血凝抑制活性及HA介导的融合抑制活性和Fc受体介导的效应功能评估,并在致死性小鼠攻击模型中评估其保护效果。通过冷冻电子显微镜技术阐明4F02结合的结构基础。筛选人血清中针对类似表位的抗体。结果:克隆4F02识别跨越数十年流行的甲型H3N2流感病毒的HA。其可中和多种H3N2病毒,血凝抑制活性较弱,但可阻断HA介导的融合活性,激活Fc受体介导的信号传导,并在小鼠致死性攻击中提供保护。冷冻电子显微镜显示,4F02靶向HA头部基部的头-茎界面,该界面跨越抗原位点C、D和E。人血清中检测到针对类似表位的抗体,但水平较低。解读:对4F02表位的表征揭示了H3-HA头-茎界面这一先前被低估的脆弱位点。该发现拓展了对保守表位的认知,并为开发能够抵御抗原变异的流感疫苗提供了靶标。资助:本研究由日本医疗研究开发机构、JSPS KAKENHI及美国国立过敏症和传染病研究所资助。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别并表征H3-HA上的保守表位,为开发能够抵御抗原变异的疫苗提供信息。多种广泛反应性人源单克隆抗体(mAb)已针对甲型流感病毒血凝素(HA)并识别出跨亚型或亚型内的保守表位。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究筛选了一组先前报道的针对H3-HA的反应性人源单克隆抗体,以识别能够识别保守表位的抗体。候选克隆4F02在体外被评估了中和活性、血凝抑制活性、HA介导的融合抑制活性以及Fc受体介导的效应功能,并在致死性小鼠攻击模型中评估了其保护效果。
analysis_zh.methods: 我们筛选了一组先前报道的针对H3血凝素(HA)的反应性人单克隆抗体(mAb),以识别识别保守表位的mAb。使用冷冻电子显微镜确定了4F02结合的结构基础。筛选了人血清以检测针对类似表位的抗体。
analysis_zh.main_results: 克隆 4F02 识别了传播数十年的人类甲型流感 (H3N2) 病毒的 HA。它能中和多种 H3N2 病毒,表现出微弱的血凝抑制作用,阻断 HA 介导的融合活性,激活 Fc 受体介导的信号传导,并保护小鼠免受致命攻击。冷冻电镜显示,4F02 靶向位于头-茎界面处的 HA 头基部,跨越抗原位点 C、D 和 E。在人类血清中检测到了针对类似表位的抗体,尽管水平较低。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 对4F02表位的特征分析揭示了H3-HA头部茎部接口处一个此前未被充分重视的保守性位点。该发现拓展了对保守表位的认知,并为开发针对季节性流感的疫苗疫苗提供了靶标,该疫苗对抗原变异具有更强的适应性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这一发现为开发对抗原变化具有弹性的流感 疫苗 提供了一个潜在靶标,这可以改善针对 季节性流感 暴发 的公共卫生准备。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖体外和小鼠模型数据而受到限制,这些数据可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是强有力的,因为它通过功能验证直接识别和表征了 H3-HA 上的保守表位。

papers.title: Functional mapping of IFITM3 resolves its antiviral core and deciphers human influenza susceptibility
papers.abstract: Genetic variation in interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) contributes to inter-individual differences in influenza outcome, yet a comprehensive functional map of IFITM3 variation remains unavailable. Here we show a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants across three influenza A strains using deep mutational scanning. Our data reveals a functionally constrained central region, providing functional evidence consistent with a Type II membrane topology and highlighting structural features associated with antiviral activity. Comparison with AlphaMissense reveals systematic limitations in predicting the effects of variants within unstructured N-terminal motifs and lipid-embedded domains. Crucially, computational models fail to recognize variants with enhanced antiviral activity, such as G133Q. By integrating this atlas with ClinVar and gnomAD, we provide a functional readout for rare human alleles that may influence susceptibility to infection. These findings provide a resource for interpreting human variation and establish a framework for studying host-directed antiviral mechanisms. This study generates a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants using deep mutational scanning. The resulting map resolves the protein’s intramembrane antiviral core and identifies key rare human alleles that dictate susceptibility to influenza infection

papers.full_text: communications biology Article A Nature Portfolio journal Article in Press https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10800-0 Functional mapping of IFITM3 resolves its antiviral core and deciphers human influenza susceptibility Check for updates Jian Chen 1 , Shufa Zheng2, Jinjin Qi1, Haibo Wu1, Hangping Yao 1 & Min Zheng 1 Genetic variation in interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) contributes to inter- individual differences in influenza outcome, yet a comprehensive functional map of IFITM3 variation remains unavailable. Here we show a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants across three influenza A strains using deep mutational scanning. Our data reveals a functionally constrained central region, providing functional evidence consistent with a Type II membrane topology and highlighting structural features associated with antiviral activity. Comparison with AlphaMissense reveals systematic limitations in predicting the effects of variants within unstructured N-terminal motifs and lipid-embedded domains. Crucially, computational models fail to recognize variants with enhanced antiviral activity, such as G133Q. By integrating this atlas with ClinVar and gnomAD, we provide a functional readout for rare human alleles that may influence susceptibility to infection. These findings provide a resource for interpreting human variation and establish a framework for studying host-directed antiviral mechanisms. Influenza A virus (IAV) infection exhibits remarkable inter-individual heterogeneity, with clinical outcomesranging from mild self-limiting illness to severe viral pneumonia and death1. Human genetic studies have increasingly revealed that this variability is shaped not only by viral factors but also by host-intrinsic antiviral defenses2–4. Among these, Interferon- induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) stands as a frontline sentinel. By blocking endosomal membrane fusion, IFITM3 restricts a diverse array of enveloped viruses, including IAV and SARS-CoV-25–9. The best- characterized example is the rs12252-C allele, which has been repeatedly associated with severe influenza and COVID-19 outcomes in multiple human cohorts, although its molecular consequences remain incompletely resolved10–14. Such associations suggest that even subtle perturbations in IFITM3 function can profoundly shift infection trajectories. Despite extensive study, the structural basis of IFITM3-mediated viral restriction remains incompletely understood. Prior studies have identified individual functional elements, including the N-terminal Y20XXΦ motif required for endolysosomal trafficking15, S-palmitoylation sites critical for membrane association16; and lysine residues that regulate protein turnover17. In addition, an amphipathic helix (residues 59–68) has been proposed to act as the core fusion-inhibitory element by altering membrane biophysical properties18. However, these “snapshot” studies leave two fundamental challenges unresolved. First, while the precise membrane topology of IFITM3 has been historically debated (with models proposing Type I, Type II, or intramembrane orientations)15,19,20, recent evidence lar- gely supports a Type II topology7,17,19,21,22. Although specific sequence motifs are known to influence its activity, the field still lacks a high-resolution functionalmapanchoredtothisphysicalstructure18,23–25.Second,theclinical interpretation of IFITM3 variation is lagging. Of the ~270 rare missense variants identified in humans, fewer than 20 are functionally classified, leaving most variants classified as of uncertain significance (VUS)26–28. Computational predictors are increasingly used to prioritize candidate pathogenic variants. However, their performance on antiviral restriction factors, particularly membrane-associated proteins such as IFITM3, remains largely untested against comprehensive experimental datasets29–32. Resolving these questions requires measurements at a scale impossible to achieve through conventional one-by-one mutagenesis. Deep mutational scanning (DMS) provides a powerful framework for experimentally mea- suring the functional consequences of protein variation in a high- throughput manner33–43. However, many prior DMS studies relied on sampling-based mutagenesis strategies or incomplete variant libraries. A fully synthesized, position-complete, and unbiased saturation landscape that captures all possible amino acid substitutions across an entire protein 1State Key Laboratory for Diagnosis and Treatment of Infectious Diseases, National Clinical Research Center for Infectious Diseases, Collaborative Innovation Center for Diagnosis and Treatment of Infectious Diseases, The First Affiliated Hospital, School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. 2Department of Laboratory Medicine, The First Affiliated Hospital, School of Medicine, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. e-mail: jianchen76@zju.edu.cn; minzheng@zju.edu.cn Communications Biology Article in Press 1234567890():,; 1234567890():,; has remained rare, particularly in the context of functional mapping of antiviral activity. Here, we employed deep mutational scanning (DMS) to generated a position-complete saturation mutagenesis library encompassing 2898 IFITM3 variants. We quantified variant fitness against three influenza A viruses, including the avian-origin H7N9 strain and two H1N1 laboratory strains (PR8 and WSN) that differ in entry and fusion requirements44. By testing these distinct viral entry pathways within a unified screening fra- mework, we: (1) reveal a mutational constraint pattern most consistent with experimentally supported Type II topology framework; (2) identify key biophysical features underlying the antiviral activity of the intramembrane domain; (3) benchmark the performance and limitations of current pathogenicity prediction models; and (4) provide an experimental frame- work for the interpretation and prioritization of IFITM3 variants identified in human populations. Results DMS of IFITM3 across multiple IAV strains and cellular contexts To map the functional determinants of IFITM3-mediated viral restriction, we executed a deep mutational scanning (DMS) screen encompassing all 133 residues under the selective pressure of influenza A virus (IAV) (Fig. 1A). We constructed two independent pooled lentiviral saturation mutagenesis libraries, comprising 2508 missense, 126 synonymous (SYN), 132 nonsense (STOP), and 132 deletion (DEL) variants. Next-generation sequencing verified plasmid library quality, showing >99% coverage of the intended variants and a uniform abundance distribution (log10 variance <0.5) (Fig. 1B, C). Following stable transduction into interferon-deficient HEK293T cells45–48 and IFITM3-null A549 cells (IFITM3-KO clone2, Supplementary Fig. 1A, B), expression of the variant libraries did not significantly affect baseline cell viability (Supplementary Fig. 1C), and library representation remained highly uniform in both cell types (Supplementary Fig. 1D). Validation assays confirmed that library-expressing cells retained antiviral activity against all three viruses (Supplementary Fig. 1E). To assess the antiviral function of each mutation, the library-expressing cells were sub- sequently challenged with three antigenically distinct influenza A virus (IAV) strains: the laboratory-adapted H1N1 strains PR8 and WSN, and a clinical avian-origin H7N9 isolate. Infected (NP + ) and uninfected (NP-) cells were isolated via fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) (Supple- mentary Fig. 1F) to quantify variant abundance shifts. We found that antiviral fitness scores derived from deep sequencing were highly repro- ducible between biological replicates (Spearman’s ρ > 0.5) (Fig. 1D–G). As expected, nonsense variants abolished antiviral activity, synonymous var- iants clustered near wild-type levels, whereas missense and deletion variants spanned a broad range of fitness scores(Fig. 1H–M). This approach enables systematic dissection of host–virus interactions at single-amino-acid resolution. The functional landscape reveals domain-specific mutational constraints To assess whether mutational effects were conserved across the influenza A virus strains examined here, variant-level fitness scores from the primary A549 dataset were visualized as mutational landscapes (Fig. 2A–C), with corresponding HEK293T datasets shown in Supplementary Fig. 2A–C. High correlations between viral datasets indicate that mutational effects on IFITM3 function are broadly conserved across the influenza A virus strains examined in this study (Supplementary Fig. 3A–F). To evaluate domain- specific sensitivity, missense variants within each structural domain were benchmarked against internal synonymous controls from the correspond- ing domain19,20 (Fig. 2D–F, Supplementary Fig. 2D–F). The N-terminal region (residues 2–55) and distal C-terminal tail (residues 131–133) exhibited comparatively lower mutational constraint than the membrane- associated core of IFITM3. However, this tolerance was not uniform, with specific functional elements remaining strongly constrained. Notably, substitutions within the conserved endocytic YXXΦ trafficking motif (residues20–23)markedlycompromisedantiviralactivity49.Conversely,the central membrane-associated core (residues 59–130), comprising the amphipathic helix (AH), conserved intracellular loop (CIL), and trans- membrane domain (TMD), displayed substantially reduced mutational tolerance. Although traditional hydropathy-based algorithms identify only residues ~59–68 as a membrane-inserted segment18, our DMS data indicate that the downstream helices (CIL and TMD) are similarly constrained, consistent with a more extended membrane-associated architecture than predicted by hydropathy-based models alone. Evolutionary conservation and DMS identify a structurally con- strained functional core within IFITM3 To examine the extent to which evolutionary conservation captures mutational tolerance, we compiled IFITM3 orthologs from 33 representa- tive vertebrate species spanning major evolutionary lineages, generated a multiple-sequence alignment (Supplementary Fig. 4, Supplementary Fig. 5A), and compared site-wise conservation scores with DMS-derived fitness measurements across IFITM3 (Fig. 3A, B). Positions exhibiting high evolutionary conservation generally displayed reduced mutational toler- ance,resultinginsignificantcorrelationsbetweenconservationandantiviral fitness across all three viral datasets (Spearman’s R = –0.67 to –0.72, P < 0.001; Fig. 3C–E), with similar relationships observed in HEK293T cells (Supplementary Fig. 5B–E). These results indicate that evolutionary con- servation is broadly associated with functional importance across IFITM3. Consistent with this relationship, several previously characterized reg- ulatory residues were among the most constrained positions in our dataset, including the palmitoylated cysteines C71, C72, and C10516, as well as ubiquitination-associated lysines K83, K84, and K10450 (Supplementary Fig. 5F). The concordance between evolutionary conservation, prior mechanistic studies, and DMS-derived fitness measurements further sup- ports the biological validity of the functional landscape generated in this study. Having established a global relationship between evolutionary con- servation and antiviral fitness, we next asked whether mutational con- straints clustered within specific regions of the IFITM3 structure. We mapped DMS fitness scores onto the experimentally validated Type II membrane topology and found that functional constraintsare concentrated within the central CD225 domain, which encompasses the majority of residues exhibiting strong intolerance to mutation (Fig. 4A). Notably, this region contains a recently proposed 53-residue R-SNARE-like motif 51. Several residues implicated in this motif, including F75, F78, R85, and G95, were highly sensitive to amino acid substitution and consistently displayed severe losses of antiviral activity (Fig. 3B). Among these, R85 corresponds to the central “0” layer residue proposed within the SNARE-like architecture and emerged as one of the most mutation-intolerant positions across the entireprotein.TheclosecorrespondencebetweentheproposedSNARE-like motifandthemutationallyconstrainedcoreidentifiedbyDMSsuggeststhat preservation of this region is a major determinant of IFITM3 antiviral activity and may reflect structural or functional requirements associated with SNARE-like interactions51. Todefinethestructuralbasisoftheseconstraints,weanalyzedthethree membrane-associated helical segments individually (designated Helices 1–3) (Fig. 4A, Supplementary Fig. 6A). Within Helix 1 (the amphipathic helix, AH), antiviral efficacy correlated strictly with amphipathic geometry52,53. To quantify this relationship, we evaluated mutation-induced alterationsinthehydrophobic moment(〈μH〉) across218single-aminoacid substitutions54 (Fig. 4B), and calculated mutation-induced changes in the hydrophobic moment (Fig. 4C). Disrupting the hydrophobic anchors (e.g., F63, L66) significantly compromised function, while introducing hydro- phobic residues onto the polar face (e.g., L62, M68) similarly abolished restriction18. Distinct outliers, such as W60 and N64, implied additional requirements beyond pure amphipathicity, likely involving interfacial aro- matic packing or specific lipid headgroup interactions23–25(Fig. 4C). Helix 2 (residues 70–88) displayed uniformly strong mutational intolerance (Fig. 4D). Unlike the amphipathic Helix 1, this segment exhibited high https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10800-0 Article Communications Biology Article in Press average hydrophobicity (〈H〉= 1.133) and a low hydrophobic moment (〈μH〉= 0.179) (Fig. 4E), consistent with a deeply membrane-embedded region extending into a structurally constrained cytosolic loop (residues 81–88) (Supplementary Fig. 6B). Particularly strong fitness defects were observed upon mutation of residues surrounding Y80 and K83, suggesting the notion that the integrity of this intramembrane region is critical for antiviral function24,55. Within Helix 3 (residues 92–130), mutational intol- erance exhibited a pronounced helical periodicity. Mapping fitness scores onto the helical wheel revealed a clear segregation of constrained and tol- erant residues onto opposite faces of the helix (Fig. 4F, G). Highly con- strained residues, including D92, G95, and K104, clustered on one face, whereas neighboring residues on the opposing face, such as V93, T94, and https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10800-0 Article Communications Biology Article in Press Q97, remained comparatively tolerant to substitution. This asymmetric distribution identifies a putative functional surface within Helix 3 and suggeststhatantiviralactivitydependsoninteractionsmediatedbyaspecific helical interface rather than the transmembrane segment as a whole53,56. Collectively, these analyses demonstrate that mutational constraints are highly structured across IFITM3 rather than uniformly distributed. Distinct classes of functional requirements emerge within different membrane- associated helices, including maintenance of amphipathic architecture in Helix 1, structural integrity of the intramembrane region in Helix 2, and a face-specific constraint pattern within Helix 3. Together, these features define the major determinants underlying IFITM3-mediated antiviral activity17,19,20,22. Experimental functional maps expose systematic limitations in AI-based pathogenicity predictors Toevaluatetherelationshipbetweenexperimentallymeasuredfitnessscores and computational variant effect prediction, we benchmarked our DMS- derived fitness scores against AlphaMissense pathogenicity predictions, which estimate the likelihood that a missense variant disrupts protein function based on evolutionary and structural information29. Across all variants, AlphaMissense scores showed a significant overall correlation with antiviral fitness, with variants classified as “likely pathogenic” generally exhibiting reduced IFITM3-mediated restriction (Fig. 5A, B). However, several classes of variants deviated substantially from this trend. In parti- cular, AlphaMissense showed limited sensitivity to functionally important residues within the disordered N- and C-terminal regions and, by design, could not identify variants with enhanced antiviral activity, highlighting the complementary value of experimental measurements. To facilitate directcomparison, we categorized DMS fitness scores into loss of antiviral activity, WT-like (tolerant), and enhanced antiviral activity classes using empirical thresholds anchored to the distributions of synon- ymous and nonsense variants (Supplementary Fig. 7A, 7B). This analysis revealed three major classes of discordance between computational and experimental assessments: (i) “benign-but-intolerant” variants, enriched within N- and C-terminal regulatory regions; (ii) “pathogenic-but-tolerant” variants, concentrated within the intramembrane domain (residues 88–110); and (iii) variants assigned ambiguous pathogenicity scores that could be functionally resolved by DMS measurements (Fig. 5C). These discordant variants were unevenly distributed across the IFITM3 sequence (Supplementary Fig. 7C, D). Notably, predictions were largely concordant within the amphipathic helix (residues 68–80), whereas variants associated with lipid-dependent interactions or topology-related constraints were more frequently misclassified. To independently evaluate discordant variants, we selected repre- sentative substitutions for individual validation (Fig. 5D, E). Immunoblot analysis demonstrated that most variants accumulated to levels comparable to wild-type IFITM3 (Fig. 5F). papers.abstract_original: Genetic variation in interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) contributes to inter-individual differences in influenza outcome, yet a comprehensive functional map of IFITM3 variation remains unavailable. Here we show a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants across three influenza A strains using deep mutational scanning. Our data reveals a functionally constrained central region, providing functional evidence consistent with a Type II membrane topology and highlighting structural features associated with antiviral activity. Comparison with AlphaMissense reveals systematic limitations in predicting the effects of variants within unstructured N-terminal motifs and lipid-embedded domains. Crucially, computational models fail to recognize variants with enhanced antiviral activity, such as G133Q. By integrating this atlas with ClinVar and gnomAD, we provide a functional readout for rare human alleles that may influence susceptibility to infection. These findings provide a resource for interpreting human variation and establish a framework for studying host-directed antiviral mechanisms. This study generates a high-resolution functional atlas of 2,898 IFITM3 variants using deep mutational scanning. The resulting map resolves the protein’s intramembrane antiviral core and identifies key rare human alleles that dictate susceptibility to influenza infection

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a high-resolution functional map of 2,898 IFITM3 variants across three influenza A strains, revealing a functionally constrained central region that aligns with a Type II membrane topology. The research highlights structural features linked to antiviral activity and identifies limitations in computational models in predicting the effects of variants in unstructured regions. The findings offer a functional readout for rare human alleles that may affect susceptibility to influenza infection, providing a resource for understanding human variation and a framework for studying host-directed antiviral mechanisms. The study contributes to the understanding of how genetic differences in IFITM3 influence influenza outcomes, but it does not address the broader implications for public health or treatment strategies.

papers.title: Within-host antigenic selection of influenza A virus dominates over stochasticity but is limited by fitness tradeoffs and timing of the immune response
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite antigenic evolution at the global scale, positive selection of influenza virus antigenic variants is not readily observed within hosts. Here, we tested the extent to which fitness tradeoffs, the timing of immune pressure, and stochastic effects impede antigenic selection within pre-immune hosts. We used genetically barcoded influenza A/Texas/50/2012 (H3N2) viruses (Tx/12) in a guinea pig model to probe these dynamics. Positive selection of an antigenic variant was reliant on a high strength of immune pressure acting early in infection. However, when fitness tradeoffs of the antigenic change were lessened, a lower strength and later introduction of immune pressure favored the antigenic variant. In all conditions, barcode dynamics revealed moderate stochastic effects. Our results suggest that stochastic evolution does not impede selection during acute influenza virus infection. The rarity of antigenic escape may instead stem from low mutational supply, fitness tradeoffs, and the intrinsic delay between infection and antibody recall.

Using a guinea pig model with genetically barcoded H3N2 viruses, the researchers found that positive selection of antigenic variants is possible when immune pressure is strong and early in infection. The findings are limited to a guinea pig model and may not fully reflect human infection dynamics, but the experimental approach provides strong evidence for the role of these factors in antigenic selection.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 尽管在全球范围内存在抗原漂移,甲型H3N2流感病毒的抗原变异体在预免疫宿主群体中并未被轻易观察到。本研究测试了适合度权衡、免疫压力时机以及随机效应在预免疫宿主群体内阻碍抗原选择的程度。我们使用了遗传条形码标记的甲型H3N2流感病毒A/德克萨斯/50/2012株(Tx/12)在豚鼠模型中探索这些动态。抗原变异体的正向选择依赖于感染早期施加的强免疫压力。然而,当抗原变化的适合度权衡减弱时,较低强度且较晚施加的免疫压力有利于抗原变异体。在所有条件下,条形码动态显示出中等程度的随机效应。研究结果表明,随机效应并未阻碍急性流感病毒感染期间的抗原选择。抗原逃逸现象罕见的原因可能更多源于低突变供应、适合度权衡以及感染与抗体回忆之间的固有延迟。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨甲型H3N2流感病毒在预免疫宿主群体内抗原选择的作用,并试图解答为何尽管全球范围内存在抗原漂移,抗原变异体仍不常被观察到这一问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用豚鼠模型,使用遗传条形码标记的甲型H3N2流感病毒A/德克萨斯/50/2012株,以测试适合度权衡、免疫压力时机及随机效应如何影响急性感染期间的抗原选择。

papers.title: Targeted degradation of Influenza a virus nucleoprotein via aptamer-based PROTACs for antiviral therapy
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) poses a serious threat to public health due to its high mutability and rapid transmissibility. The viral nucleoprotein (NP), a highly conserved and essential component, has emerged as an ideal target for antiviral therapies. However, its biological function has proven challenging to modulate with conventional drugs, and no NP-targeting therapeutics have reached the market so far. Here, we report the development and application of an aptamer-based proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) for the targeted degradation of IAV NP. Utilizing the Direct-to-Biology (D2B) platform, we efficiently screened and identified NP-PROTAC#4 as a functional candidate. Subsequently, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation of NP‐PROTAC#4 (LNP@NP‐PROTAC#4) for effective intracellular delivery. Importantly, LNP@NP-PROTAC#4 demonstrated potent antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, NP-PROTAC#4 exerts its antiviral effects by targeting and degrading NP via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In conclusion, our findings provide the first evidence that NP-targeted PROTAC degrader exhibits therapeutic effects, proposing a novel therapeutic strategy for IAV.

Utilizing the Direct-to-Biology (D2B) platform, we efficiently screened and identified NP-PROTAC#4 as a functional candidate. Subsequently, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation of NP‐PROTAC#4 (LNP@NP‐PROTAC#4) for effective intracellular delivery. Importantly, LNP@NP-PROTAC#4 demonstrated potent antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, NP-PROTAC#4 exerts its antiviral effects by targeting and degrading NP via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In conclusion, our findings provide the first evidence that NP-targeted PROTAC degrader exhibits therapeutic effects, proposing a novel therapeutic strategy for IAV.

papers.title: Conserved influenza A epitope candidate regions and a benchmark of ESM-2 sequence features
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus antigenic drift forces annual vaccine reformulation, motivating the search for conserved epitope candidates that could support broadly protective vaccines. We systematically screened influenza A virus sequences (H1N1, H3N2, H5N1; nine viral proteins) to define 98 conserved candidate regions, 38 of which were identical across the H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1 consensus sequences, all in the polymerase complex and nucleoprotein (PB2, PB1, PA, NP), whereas the ten surface-glycoprotein (HA/NA) candidates were subtype-specific. We then benchmarked two protein-language-model (ESM-2) features against alignment conservation. Group-masked log-probability correlated moderately with MSA conservation (Spearman rho = 0.25 to 0.39 for HA) but provided no incremental value for T-cell epitope discrimination (change in AUROC +0.004, p = 0.46); attention-derived contact-density was not a valid solvent-accessibility proxy. A curated antibody-epitope benchmark (22 clusters, 5 neutralization-supported) was underpowered for a high-confidence B-cell test. We document data-quality and reproducibility pitfalls (length heterogeneity, coordinate mapping, and pseudoreplication) and release the auditable benchmark. These results provide an auditable candidate resource and show that, in the evaluated benchmarks, ESM-2 sequence scores did not improve epitope prioritization beyond alignment-derived conservation.

We document data-quality and reproducibility pitfalls (length heterogeneity, coordinate mapping, and pseudoreplication) and release the auditable benchmark. papers.abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒 抗原漂移 迫使每年重新配制 疫苗,从而激发了对可支持广泛保护性 疫苗 的保守表位候选者的搜索。我们系统地筛选了甲型流感病毒序列(H1N1、H3N2、H5N1;九种病毒蛋白),以确定 98 个保守候选区域,其中 38 个在 H1N1、H3N2 和 H5N1 共有序列中是相同的,全部位于聚合酶复合物和核蛋白(PB2、PB1、PA、NP)中,而 10 个表面糖蛋白(HA/NA)候选区域是亚型特异性的。然后,我们对两个蛋白质语言模型 (ESM-2) 特征与对齐保守性进行了基准测试。组屏蔽对数概率与 MSA 保守性适度相关(HA 的 Spearman rho = 0.25 至 0.39),但没有为 T 细胞表位辨别提供增量值(AUROC 的变化 +0.004,p = 0.46);注意力衍生的接触密度并不是有效的溶剂可及性代理。精心设计的抗体表位基准(22 个簇,5 个支持中和)对于高置信度 B 细胞测试来说动力不足。我们记录数据质量和可重复性缺陷(长度异质性、坐标映射和伪复制)并发布可审核的基准。这些结果提供了可审核的候选资源,并表明,在评估的基准中,ESM-2 序列评分并没有改善除比对衍生的保护之外的表位优先顺序。

papers.title: Severe co-infection with influenza A virus H3N2 and community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus in a child presenting with septic shock, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and necrotizing pneumonia: a rare case report
papers.abstract: Background Influenza co-infection with Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) can cause rapidly fatal necrotizing pneumonia, septic shock, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in children. Although methicillin-resistant S. aureus is often highlighted, community-acquired methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (CA-MSSA) can also produce equally severe disease. Case presentation We report an 8-year-4-month-old male with influenza A (H3N2) who developed septic shock and refractory hypoxemia, requiring immediate intubation. Due to persisting respiratory failure despite maximal ventilation, veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) was initiated on day 1. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing identified S. aureus as the dominant pathogen, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture later confirmed MSSA. After vancomycin failed clinically, the regimen was switched to linezolid. However, on day 15 of linezolid therapy, the patient developed severe linezolid-induced lactic acidosis (LILA), which resolved within 3 days of stopping the drug. The clinical course was further complicated by pneumothorax and multidrug-resistant organism superinfections. After 54 days of intensive care, the patient was discharged in good condition. Conclusion This case underscores that during influenza seasons, early empirical anti-staphylococcal therapy should be considered in children with rapidly progressive pneumonia and shock, even when CA-MSSA is suspected. Additionally, routine lactate monitoring is critical during linezolid therapy to enable prompt recognition and management of life-threatening LILA.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to highlight the potential severity of co-infection with influenza A virus H3N2 and community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus in children, as such co-infections can lead to rapidly fatal necrotizing pneumonia, septic shock, and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a rare case report describing an 8-year-4-month-old male child who developed septic shock and refractory hypoxemia due to co-infection with influenza A (H3N2) and community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. The patient required immediate intubation and was treated with linezolid, which later led to severe linezolid-induced lactic acidosis.
analysis.methods: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing was used to identify the dominant pathogen, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid culture confirmed the presence of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. The patient's clinical course was managed with anti-staphylococcal therapy and monitored for complications such as lactic acidosis.
analysis.main_results: The patient developed septic shock and refractory hypoxemia, necessitating intubation and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) on day 1. Despite treatment with linezolid, the patient experienced severe linezolid-induced lactic acidosis, which resolved after discontinuation of the drug. The patient was eventually discharged in good condition after 54 days of intensive care.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that during influenza seasons, early empirical anti-staphylococcal therapy should be considered in children with rapidly progressive pneumonia and shock, even when community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus is suspected. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for vigilance in diagnosing and treating co-infections involving influenza A (H3N2) and community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus in children, particularly during influenza seasons. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As a rare case report, the study lacks the statistical power and generalizability of larger cohort studies. analysis.summary_en: This case report describes an 8-year-old child with influenza A (H3N2) who developed severe septic shock and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to co-infection with community-acquired methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. The patient required immediate intubation and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) on day 1. Despite treatment with linezolid, the patient developed severe linezolid-induced lactic acidosis, which resolved after discontinuation. The case underscores the importance of early empirical anti-staphylococcal therapy in children with rapidly progressive pneumonia and shock during influenza seasons, and highlights the need for routine lactate monitoring during linezolid therapy to detect and manage life-threatening complications. The study provides valuable insights into the clinical management of severe influenza-related co-infections but is limited by its rarity and lack of generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在强调儿童甲型流感病毒 H3N2 和社区获得性甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌混合感染的潜在严重性,因为此类混合感染可导致迅速致命的坏死性肺炎、感染性休克和急性呼吸窘迫综合征 (ARDS)。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为一罕见病例报告,描述一名8岁4个月男童因感染甲型H3N2流感病毒与社区获得性耐甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌重症合并感染,出现脓毒性休克及难治性低氧血症。患者需立即行气管插管,并接受利奈唑胺治疗,后因严重利奈唑胺诱导性乳酸性酸中毒而中断用药。
elements_zh.methods: 使用宏基因组下一代测序来鉴定主要病原体,支气管肺泡灌洗液培养证实存在甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌。患者的临床病程通过抗葡萄球菌治疗进行管理,并监测乳酸性酸中毒等并发症。
elements_zh.main_results: 患者出现脓毒性休克及难治性低氧血症,需行气管插管并在第1天启动静脉-静脉体外膜肺氧合(VV-ECMO)。尽管接受利奈唑胺治疗,患者仍出现严重利奈唑胺诱导性乳酸性酸中毒,停药后症状缓解。患者最终于54天后康复出院。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在流感季节,对于儿童快速进展性肺炎及休克患者,即使疑似社区获得性耐甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌感染,也应考虑早期经验性抗葡萄球菌治疗。本病例强调识别并处理利奈唑胺治疗相关严重并发症的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提示,在流感季节,需警惕诊断并治疗儿童甲型H3N2流感病毒与社区获得性耐甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌合并感染。强调利奈唑胺治疗期间常规监测血乳酸水平,以便及时发现并处理危及生命的乳酸性酸中毒。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作为一项罕见的 病例报告,该研究缺乏大型 队列研究 研究的统计功效和普遍性。然而,所描述的具体病例的证据是强有力的,并且研​​究结果与管理严重流感相关合并感染的临床实践相关。

analysis_zh.main_results: 患者出现脓毒性休克及难治性低氧血症,需行气管插管并在第1天启动静脉-静脉体外膜肺氧合(VV-ECMO)。尽管接受利奈唑胺治疗,患者仍出现严重利奈唑胺诱导性乳酸性酸中毒,停药后症状缓解。患者最终于54天后康复出院。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在流感季节,对于儿童快速进展性肺炎及休克患者,即使疑似社区获得性耐甲氧西林敏感金黄色葡萄球菌感染,也应考虑早期经验性抗葡萄球菌治疗。本病例强调识别并处理利奈唑胺治疗相关严重并发症的重要性。

papers.title: ICU admission and mortality in adult patients with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09-related pneumonia in Vietnam since the 2009 H1N1 pandemic: A 10-year cohort study
papers.abstract: Background The A(H1N1)pdm09 virus remains an important cause of severe influenza worldwide. This study examined the burden of ICU admission, mortality, and associated predictors among adults with A(H1N1)pdm09-related pneumonia treated at a leading infectious diseases hospital in Vietnam. Methods Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were retrospectively collected from the medical records of adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed A(H1N1)pdm09 infection between 2009 and 2019. Results Among 729 patients with laboratory-confirmed A(H1N1)pdm09 infection, 21.7% (158/729) developed pneumonia. Among patients with pneumonia, 36.7% developed moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, 15.2% required invasive ventilation, 48.7% were admitted to the ICU, and 8.2% died. Independent predictors of ICU admission included age older than 60 years (AOR 18.91, 95% CI 3.60–99.24), the presence of comorbidities (AOR 9.39, 95% CI 2.75–32.06), and laboratory evidence of systemic inflammation, renal dysfunction, and hepatic involvement. Intensified antiviral therapy (AOR = 8.577, 95%CI 1.416–83.341, P = 0.020), and invasive ventilation (AOR 8.426, 95%CI 1.105–141.366, P = 0.039) were independently associated with mortality. Conclusions Mortality associated with A(H1N1)pdm09-related pneumonia remains substantial. Older patients, those with comorbidities, and those presenting with abnormal laboratory findings should be monitored closely for deterioration requiring intensive care. The study did not demonstrate improved outcomes with intensified antiviral regimens. Prospective studies are required before definitive treatment recommendations can be made.

papers.title: Intranasal delivery of a COBRA-based protein vaccine adjuvanted with c-di-AMP enhances breadth of protective immune responses against seasonal influenza viruses
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccines provide variable protection against antigenically drifted influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viruses. Broadly protective approaches using computationally optimized broadly reactive antigens (COBRAs) can enhance immunity against diverse strains. Bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric adenosine monophosphate (c-di-AMP) is a mucosal adjuvant that boosts vaccine-induced immune responses. Here, we hypothesized that intranasal multivalent COBRA hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) vaccination with c-di-AMP would induce broad humoral and cellular immunity in mice. Immunologically naïve and pre-immune DBA/2J mice were intranasally immunized with pentavalent vaccine formulations containing COBRA recombinant HA and NA or corresponding wild-type antigens. Formulations were administered at low or high antigen doses, with or without the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP. Humoral and cellular immune responses were evaluated, along with protection following influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viral challenge. Pentavalent COBRA HA/NA intranasal vaccination adjuvanted with c-di-AMP induced strong humoral and cellular immune responses in murine models. Vaccination induced robust, dose-dependent total IgG and hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers, along with high frequencies of antigen-specific antibody-secreting cells and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-producing cells in pre-immune mice. Naïve mice were also seroprotected mainly against H1N1 at higher vaccine doses. Following lethal challenge with H1N1, H3N2, and influenza B viruses, vaccinated mice exhibited reduced weight loss, decreased lung viral titers, and enhanced survival, with the strongest protection observed in adjuvanted groups across both naïve and pre-immune models. These findings highlight the value of combining broadly protective COBRA vaccine candidates with advanced mucosal adjuvants to enhance efficacy against antigenically drifted influenza virus strains.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza vaccines show variable protection against antigenically drifted influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viruses, creating a need for broadly protective vaccine strategies. The study aimed to test whether intranasal multivalent COBRA hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) vaccination adjuvanted with c-di-AMP could induce broad humoral and cellular immunity in mice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used immunologically naïve and pre-immune DBA/2J mice intranasally immunized with pentavalent vaccine formulations containing COBRA recombinant HA and NA or wild-type antigens. Formulations were administered at low or high antigen doses, with or without the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP.
analysis.methods: Humoral and cellular immune responses were evaluated, along with protection following influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viral challenge. The study assessed total IgG and hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers, antigen-specific antibody-secreting cells, and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-producing cells.
analysis.main_results: Following lethal challenge with H1N1, H3N2, and influenza B viruses, vaccinated mice exhibited reduced weight loss, decreased lung viral titers, and enhanced survival. The strongest protection was observed in adjuvanted groups across both naïve and pre-immune models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that combining broadly protective COBRA vaccine candidates with the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP enhanced efficacy against antigenically drifted influenza virus strains. They highlighted the value of this approach for inducing broad humoral and cellular immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that intranasal COBRA-based protein vaccination with c-di-AMP could inform the development of next-generation influenza vaccines with broader protection against seasonal strains. The approach may address limitations of current vaccines in antigenically drifted settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in murine models, limiting direct translation to humans. While the evidence demonstrates robust immunogenicity and protection in mice, further research is needed to validate these findings in human clinical trials and assess long-term efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated intranasal pentavalent COBRA hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) vaccination adjuvanted with c-di-AMP in mice to address the variable protection of seasonal influenza vaccines against drifted strains. Immunologically naïve and pre-immune DBA/2J mice received formulations at low or high doses with or without the mucosal adjuvant. Humoral and cellular immune responses were measured, including total IgG, HAI titers, antibody-secreting cells, and IFN-γ-producing cells. Following lethal challenge with H1N1, H3N2, and influenza B viruses, vaccinated mice showed reduced weight loss, lower lung viral titers, and improved survival, with the strongest protection in adjuvanted groups. The authors concluded that combining COBRA vaccines with c-di-AMP enhances breadth of immunity against antigenically drifted strains. These findings support the potential of intranasal COBRA-based protein vaccination with c-di-AMP to inform next-generation influenza vaccines, though murine model limitations necessitate human clinical validation.

papers.title_zh: 鼻内给药含c-di-AMP佐剂的COBRA基蛋白疫苗可增强对季节性流感病毒的广泛保护作用
papers.source_body_en: Seasonal influenza vaccines provide variable protection against antigenically drifted influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viruses. Broadly protective approaches using computationally optimized broadly reactive antigens (COBRAs) can enhance immunity against diverse strains. Bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric adenosine monophosphate (c-di-AMP) is a mucosal adjuvant that boosts vaccine-induced immune responses. Here, we hypothesized that intranasal multivalent COBRA hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) vaccination with c-di-AMP would induce broad humoral and cellular immunity in mice. Immunologically naïve and pre-immune DBA/2J mice were intranasally immunized with pentavalent vaccine formulations containing COBRA recombinant HA and NA or corresponding wild-type antigens. Formulations were administered at low or high antigen doses, with or without the mucosal adjuvant c-di-AMP. Humoral and cellular immune responses were evaluated, along with protection following influenza A (H1N1 and H3N2) and influenza B viral challenge. Pentavalent COBRA HA/NA intranasal vaccination adjuvanted with c-di-AMP induced strong humoral and cellular immune responses in murine models. Vaccination induced robust, dose-dependent total IgG and hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers, along with high frequencies of antigen-specific antibody-secreting cells and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-producing cells in pre-immune mice. Naïve mice were also seroprotected mainly against H1N1 at higher vaccine doses. Following lethal challenge with H1N1, H3N2, and influenza B viruses, vaccinated mice exhibited reduced weight loss, decreased lung viral titers, and enhanced survival, with the strongest protection observed in adjuvanted groups across both naïve and pre-immune models. These findings highlight the value of combining broadly protective COBRA vaccine candidates with advanced mucosal adjuvants to enhance efficacy against antigenically drifted influenza virus strains.
papers.abstract_zh: 季节性流感 疫苗 针对抗原漂移的甲型流感(H1N1 和 H3N2)和乙型流感病毒提供可变保护。使用计算优化的广泛反应性抗原(COBRA)的广泛保护方法可以增强针对不同菌株的免疫力。双-(3',5')-环状二聚腺苷单磷酸 (c-di-AMP) 是一种粘膜佐剂,可增强 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答。在这里,我们假设鼻内多价 COBRA 血凝素 (HA) 和神经氨酸酶 (NA) 疫苗接种 与 c-di-AMP 会诱导小鼠广泛的体液和细胞免疫。用含有 COBRA 重组 HA 和 NA 或相应野生型抗原的五价 疫苗 制剂对免疫学上未接触过的和免疫前的 DBA/2J 小鼠进行鼻内免疫。制剂以低或高抗原剂量施用,有或没有粘膜佐剂c-di-AMP。评估了体液和细胞 免疫应答,以及甲型流感(H1N1 和 H3N2)和乙型流感病毒攻击后的保护作用。五价 COBRA HA/NA 鼻内 疫苗接种 与 c-di-AMP 佐剂在小鼠模型中诱导强体液和细胞 免疫应答。疫苗接种 在免疫前小鼠中诱导出强劲的、剂量依赖性的总 IgG 和血凝抑制 (HAI) 滴度,以及高频率的抗原特异性抗体分泌细胞和干扰素 γ (IFN-γ) 产生细胞。在较高的 疫苗 剂量下,首次实验的小鼠也主要针对 H1N1 病毒而获得血清保护。在遭受 H1N1、H3N2 和 B 型流感病毒的致命攻击后,接种疫苗的小鼠表现出体重减轻减轻、肺部病毒滴度降低和存活率提高,在幼稚模型和免疫前模型中,在佐剂组中观察到最强的保护作用。这些发现凸显了将具有广泛保护性的 COBRA 疫苗 候选药物与先进的粘膜佐剂相结合,以增强针对抗原漂移流感病毒株的功效的价值。
