IANS Created On: 24 Aug 2026 11:22 AM ISTComment Share : X Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital fully equipped to manage H1N1 cases, seasonal illnesses A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON Google News New Delhi: Safdarjung Hospital in Delhi has said it is fully equipped to manage patients suffering from swine flu, or H1N1 influenza, as well as other seasonal illnesses, with necessary medicines, treatment facilities and supportive care available. In a statement, the hospital said patients presenting with influenza-like symptoms are being appropriately assessed and fast-tracked for timely medical attention. Treatment is being provided according to the clinical requirements of individual patients and prevailing medical guidelines. “The hospital is fully equipped to manage cases of swine flu and other seasonal illnesses, with necessary medicines, treatment facilities and supportive care available,” the hospital said. “Patients presenting with influenza-like symptoms are appropriately assessed and fast-tracked for timely medical attention. Appropriate treatment is provided as per clinical requirements and prevailing guidelines,” it added. The hospital further said it continues to monitor such cases and has adequate arrangements in place for their management. The statement comes amid increased attention on H1N1 and seasonal influenza cases in Delhi. Health authorities and hospitals have been closely monitoring patients reporting influenza-like symptoms, particularly those requiring timely medical intervention because of breathing difficulties or other complications. Safdarjung Hospital said its existing arrangements are adequate to manage such patients and provide supportive care wherever required. The hospital’s emphasis remains on early assessment, timely treatment and continued monitoring of influenza-like illnesses. H1N1 is a subtype of influenza A virus that causes respiratory infection. It became widely known as “swine flu” during the 2009 influenza pandemic. The virus subsequently became part of the seasonal influenza viruses that circulate among humans. Common symptoms of influenza can include fever, cough, sore throat, headache, body aches, fatigue and a runny or blocked nose. In many cases, people recover within several days to about a week. However, influenza can sometimes lead to serious complications, particularly among older adults, young children, pregnant women and people with certain underlying health conditions. Severe respiratory symptoms, persistent high fever, breathing difficulty, chest discomfort, confusion or a worsening condition may require prompt medical evaluation. Influenza spreads mainly through respiratory droplets and particles released when an infected person coughs, sneezes or talks. Maintaining good hand hygiene, covering coughs and sneezes and avoiding close contact with people who are unwell can help reduce transmission. Seasonal influenza vaccination is also an important preventive measure, particularly for people at higher risk of complications. ICMR sources said the influenza strains currently circulating in the country are “well matched with the vaccine strains recommended for the Northern Hemisphere”. The circulating Influenza A (H1N1) pdm09 viruses belong to the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like strain. They are part of clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, and have been circulating since 2025. Seasonal influenza, including H1N1, is generally self-limiting. Fever, cough, headache and body ache are among the common symptoms, with most people recovering with appropriate care and rest. Young children, older people and those with underlying medical conditions face a higher risk of complications. Also Read - Rain brings Delhi-NCR to standstill Advertisement The national capital has reported more than 2,300 Influenza-A cases this year, including over 1,777 H1N1 cases till Friday. The Delhi health department reported 114 H1N1 cases on Thursday alone. The Delhi government has advised people to maintain respiratory hygiene, avoid crowded places and seek medical advice without delay when required. Union Health Minister J P Nadda reviewed the H1N1 situation and preparedness across the country on Friday, with particular attention to Delhi. Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh also attended the meeting. Nadda reviewed national surveillance and epidemiological trends, influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) patterns, testing and laboratory surveillance. He also assessed healthcare preparedness, including hospital beds, critical care and oxygen-supported beds, ventilators, essential medicines, diagnostics and other supplies. The ICMR sources said the situation is being monitored through regular surveillance. They advised people to consult a doctor if symptoms persist, worsen or become severe. Nadda also called for close monitoring and early detection and management of any unusual increase or clustering of cases. Written By Fareha Naaz Updated24 Aug 2026, 10:16 AM IST H1N1 Cases near 1,800 in Delhi: Why Is the Health Minister Holding a Meeting Today? Explained AI Quick Read A survey conducted across Delhi NCR recently revealed that residents of around 54% households have members infected with flu, showing viral fever like symptoms at a time when H1N1 cases are on the rise. The findings of this Local Circles report published on 23 August are based on 32,000 responses collected from across Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. Around 69% respondents were men and 31% were women. The survey further revealed that 23% households surveyed have four or more individuals currently down with flu fever like symptoms. Around 16% of the respondents were reported to have two to three symptomatic members while 15% households surveyed had at least one individual down with viral like fever. This suggests sustained transmission inside homes, implying that 39% of households surveyed had two or more members symptomatic at the same time. With seasonal influenza in focus due to surge in cases, Delhi reported 2,392 influenza-A cases this year. This year, Delhi's cumulative swine flu tally has reached 1,777 with H1N1 being the predominant strain. At the same while H1 cases tally stood at 37, H3 at 138 and other influenza cases at 440. Also Read | H1N1 cases in Delhi higher, ‘severe’: Experts warn, advisory issued | 10 points It should be noted that the official case count includes only citizens who visited a hospital or laboratory to be tested. There is a shortfall in reported figures as many others who contracted the disease but recovered at home remain unaccounted. ICMR issues statement on H1N1 virus In the wake of rising swine flu cases, the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) issued a statement on Sunday, clarifying that no new strain of influenza A (H1N1) has been identified in the country. ICMR scientists emphasized that there is no cause for panic regarding the seasonal influenza virus currently circulating. With many Delhi-NCR residents suffering from fever, cough, sore throat, headache, body aches, chills and fatigue, ICMR called the seasonal influenza "mostly self-limiting".
